standard.name: AI Sloppy Copy Standard
standard.term_match: case-insensitive; hyphen and whitespace forms are equivalent; family datasets scan common grammatical forms and listed phrase variants
standard.enforcement: hard terms and patterns block release; warnings and review rules appear in requested compliance reports
standard.protected_text: fenced code, inline code, Markdown block quotes, URLs, exact allow-list entries, and approved glossary entries

source_register.update_policy: Pinned revisions only. New source revisions require review, tests, a version change, and release notes.

categories.name: Hedge words
categories.instruction: Remove unspecific hedges. Keep a qualifier only when the evidence requires one.
categories.replacement_strategy: State the bounded fact. Use a measured qualifier such as 'In the 4 cases tested' when needed.

categories.name: AI bridge phrases
categories.instruction: Remove transitions that do not state a real relationship between ideas.
categories.replacement_strategy: Start the next sentence with its subject and action.

categories.name: Closing summaries
categories.instruction: Do not end with a recap that repeats the preceding content.
categories.replacement_strategy: End with one specific next action, callback, or supported closing point.

categories.name: Marketing speak
categories.instruction: Remove corporate promotion and empty jargon.
categories.replacement_strategy: Name the literal action or result. Delete the sentence when its plain version says nothing.

categories.name: Vague authority claims
categories.instruction: Do not imply outside support without naming the source.
categories.replacement_strategy: Cite the study, person, dataset, or decision record. Otherwise remove the authority claim.

categories.name: Not-just-X-but-Y constructions
categories.instruction: Ban the literal phrase 'not just' and close variants used for escalation.
categories.replacement_strategy: Delete the first clause and state the supported second clause directly.

categories.name: Dash ban
categories.instruction: Do not use em dashes or en dashes in authored prose.
categories.replacement_strategy: Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses.

categories.name: Tricolons
categories.replacement_strategy: Allow one per 500 words. Rewrite excess lists as one, two, or four supported points.

prohibited_patterns.name: In-a-world-where drama
prohibited_patterns.formula: In a world where [broad change], [virtue] becomes [advantage].
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Delete the cinematic setup. State the specific condition and business effect.

prohibited_patterns.name: Most-people-versus-few split
prohibited_patterns.formula: Most people [weak behavior]. The few or best [approved behavior].
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Remove the invented social split. Name the observed behavior, source, and result.

prohibited_patterns.name: Stop-start switch
prohibited_patterns.formula: Stop [old habit]. Start [new habit].
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Replace the command pair with one specific action and its reason.

prohibited_patterns.name: Not-this-not-that-but-this triple
prohibited_patterns.formula: It is not X. It is not Y. It is Z.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Delete the strawmen. State the supported point directly.

prohibited_patterns.name: Already-behind fear claim
prohibited_patterns.formula: If you are not doing X, you are already behind or losing.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Remove the threat. State the measured cost, deadline, or known risk.

prohibited_patterns.name: The-real-work reveal
prohibited_patterns.formula: The real work, game, or battle is not X. It is Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: State the actual task and why it matters without a reveal setup.

prohibited_patterns.name: You-do-not-need-more smack
prohibited_patterns.formula: You do not need more X. You need Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Replace the claim with the exact missing resource, action, or decision.

prohibited_patterns.name: Never-easier-never-harder paradox
prohibited_patterns.formula: It has never been easier to X. It has never been harder to Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Remove the era-wide comparison. Use current facts and a bounded claim.

prohibited_patterns.name: Fake truth reveal
prohibited_patterns.formula: Here is the truth: X. What nobody tells you is X.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Delete the reveal label. State the fact and its source.

prohibited_patterns.name: Not-about-but-about redefinition
prohibited_patterns.formula: It is not about X, but about Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Remove the contrast wrapper. State Y only when the evidence supports it.

prohibited_patterns.name: Not-about-it-is-about contrast
prohibited_patterns.formula: It is not about X. It is about Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Remove the contrast wrapper and state the supported point directly.

prohibited_patterns.name: Not-just-it-is contrast
prohibited_patterns.formula: It is not just X. It is Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Delete the setup and state the specific supported claim.

prohibited_patterns.name: That-is-not-that-is contrast
prohibited_patterns.formula: That is not X. That is Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: State the classification and its evidence without the scripted correction.

prohibited_patterns.name: Not-because-but-because pair
prohibited_patterns.formula: Not because X. But because Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Write one complete causal sentence supported by the facts.

prohibited_patterns.name: Not-by-but-by contrast
prohibited_patterns.formula: Not by doing X, but by doing Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: State the action that caused the result and remove the staged contrast.

prohibited_patterns.name: No-no-just triple
prohibited_patterns.formula: No X. No Y. Just Z.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Replace the fragment stack with one direct sentence.

prohibited_patterns.name: Three staged fragments
prohibited_patterns.formula: X. Y. Z.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Review three adjacent fragments used as a slogan and rewrite them as a normal sentence or supported list.

prohibited_patterns.name: And-the-question-answer
prohibited_patterns.formula: And the X? Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Remove the staged question and state the answer in a complete sentence.

prohibited_patterns.name: Result-or-outcome question reveal
prohibited_patterns.formula: The result? Y. The outcome? Y.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: State the measured result in a normal sentence.

prohibited_patterns.name: Repeated one-or-two-word fragments
prohibited_patterns.formula: Two-word fragments repeated two or three times.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Review adjacent short fragments used for cadence and rewrite them as a normal sentence or supported list.

prohibited_patterns.name: AI-detector passage guarantee
prohibited_patterns.formula: This will pass an AI detector or is guaranteed human-written.
prohibited_patterns.instruction: Do not promise detector passage or authorship probability. Report rule compliance and source-backed review status only.

style_rules.name: Em-dash and en-dash ban
style_rules.instruction: Do not use em dashes or en dashes in authored prose. Replace them with periods, commas, colons, semicolons, or parentheses.

style_rules.name: Staged ellipsis line
style_rules.instruction: Delete the pause and continue with the next useful sentence.

style_rules.name: Excessive period run
style_rules.instruction: Replace the period run with one normal punctuation mark.

style_rules.name: Performative aside
style_rules.instruction: Delete the interruption unless it carries required information.

style_rules.name: Stacked short fragments
style_rules.instruction: Combine staged one-line fragments into a normal paragraph. Keep fragments only when the audience or format requires them.

style_rules.name: Unsupported universal claim
style_rules.instruction: Replace claims about everyone, nobody, winners, or the future with a sourced and bounded statement.

style_rules.name: Thesaurus substitution
style_rules.instruction: Do not replace a prohibited word with another promotional abstraction. Rewrite the sentence around facts, actions, owners, dates, numbers, or decisions.

style_rules.name: Tricolon rate cap
style_rules.instruction: Use no more than one three-part rhetorical list per 500 words. Rewrite excess lists as one, two, or four supported points.

style_rules.name: Decorative emoji
style_rules.instruction: Remove decorative emoji unless the user explicitly requested emoji.

style_rules.name: Chatbot closing
style_rules.instruction: Delete canned offers and close with the requested answer or next action.

style_rules.name: Title-case heading
style_rules.instruction: Use sentence case unless a required name, UI label, or template uses title case.

style_rules.name: Decorative formatting
style_rules.instruction: Keep bold, lists, and tables only when they help the reader scan or compare information.

style_rules.name: Hyphenated pair repetition
style_rules.instruction: Remove repeated decorative compound pairs. Keep standard technical compounds.

style_rules.name: Hidden actor
style_rules.instruction: Name the actor when known. Keep passive voice when the actor is unknown or irrelevant.

style_rules.name: Rhetorical opener
style_rules.instruction: Replace the staged question with the concrete point unless the question serves the requested format.

style_rules.name: Staccato punchline
style_rules.instruction: Join staged fragments into normal prose unless short fragments match the user's requested voice.

style_rules.name: Aphoristic contrast
style_rules.instruction: State the supported claim without a slogan-like reversal.

style_rules.name: Generic positive conclusion
style_rules.instruction: Delete generic approval or replace it with a specific action, result, or unresolved question.

style_rules.name: Generic challenges and future close
style_rules.instruction: Name the specific unresolved issue, owner, date, and next action.

style_rules.name: Copula avoidance
style_rules.instruction: Use a direct form of 'be' when it states the relationship more plainly.

style_rules.name: Significance claim
style_rules.instruction: Remove unsupported claims about importance, legacy, or a wider movement. State the observed result.

style_rules.name: Superficial participial add-on
style_rules.instruction: Remove an '-ing' add-on when it only restates importance or consequence.

style_rules.name: Promotional tone
style_rules.instruction: Replace sales language with verifiable attributes, limits, prices, dates, or results.

style_rules.name: Vague attribution
style_rules.instruction: Name the source and citation or remove the authority claim.

style_rules.name: False range
style_rules.instruction: Use a range only when the endpoints define a real scale or sequence.

style_rules.name: Synonym cycling
style_rules.instruction: Repeat the precise noun when alternate labels would blur the subject.

style_rules.name: Diff-anchored writing
style_rules.instruction: Write for the reader's task, not as a narration of edits or prompt history.

style_rules.name: Fragmented header sequence
style_rules.instruction: Combine tiny sections when each heading contains only one sentence or fragment.

style_rules.name: Missing writer basis
style_rules.instruction: For recommendations, testimonials, case studies, and first-person endorsements, state how the named writer knows the subject and what the writer directly observed. Ask for missing facts or name the gap outside the draft.

style_rules.name: Evidence-free praise
style_rules.instruction: Support material judgments with a verified firsthand incident, decision, or measured result. Do not turn a resume into praise one credential at a time.

style_rules.name: Manufactured human texture
style_rules.instruction: Do not add typos, random sentence variation, slang, personal memories, sensory details, or opinions solely to appear human or lower a detector score.

style_rules.name: Unapproved voice imitation
style_rules.instruction: Use only owner-approved voice samples and recorded preferences. Do not infer a person's private voice from demographics, job title, or relationship.

style_rules.name: Uniform summary cadence
style_rules.instruction: Review long-form prose with evenly sized paragraphs, repeated sentence openings, or credential-by-credential sequencing. Rebuild from the writer's purpose and strongest evidence instead of adding random variation.

style_rules.name: Authorship-detector claim
style_rules.instruction: Do not report an AI probability or promise passage of an AI detector. Report rule compliance, evidence coverage, voice-source status, and owner approval separately.

style_rules.name: Ad intent routing
style_rules.instruction: Activate paid ad mode when the requested deliverable is ad copy or ad creative for any advertising platform. Do not activate it for reporting, analysis, or operations work that only mentions ads or ad spend.

style_rules.name: Hook or callout required
style_rules.instruction: Start each complete ad with a Hook or Callout suited to the audience and awareness stage. For one complete ad, return the finished ad plus three hook options unless the user asks for one module only.

style_rules.name: Value block order
style_rules.instruction: Build the Value section in this order: Problem and Promise; Mechanism and verified Proof; Offer Snapshot and Risk. Define the value being shown. Define who should see it. State when it matters. A product feature does not prove a customer problem or before-state. Do not reverse-engineer either from the solution. Missing proof must produce a source-bounded draft with the evidence gap named outside the ad.

style_rules.name: Direct CTA
style_rules.instruction: End a complete ad with exactly one direct CTA that names the action and its immediate benefit. The entire ad may contain only that action request. Remove secondary invitations such as learn more or see how. Also remove try it, get started, compare, and discover. Verify any stated time frame before use. Keep each duration attached to the exact supplied event. Do not convert a call duration into a delivery time or workflow duration. Do not convert it into a result time or promised outcome. If only a call duration is known, keep it out of hooks and benefit claims. State only that the call takes that long or use the event name in the CTA. Do not invent what occurs during the call.

style_rules.name: Campaign consistency
style_rules.instruction: Keep one CTA fixed across a campaign. Use three to five Value blocks and a larger hook bank across approved awareness stages. Do not change the funnel action between variants unless the user changes the campaign goal.

style_rules.name: Platform adaptation
style_rules.instruction: Map Hook, Value, and CTA into the current fields, placement, format, and limits of the requested platform. Current platform requirements and verified offer facts outrank a template.

style_rules.name: Ad evidence and rights
style_rules.instruction: An ad may use only supplied, verified facts. Do not infer product behavior or delivery method. Do not infer automation or compatibility. Do not invent the before-state or pain intensity. Do not invent workflow details or customer results. Never invent proof or testimonials. Do not invent urgency or offer facts. Verify usage rights and platform limits before publication. State a Problem or Promise only when supported. If a required block lacks facts, omit the claim or use a bounded placeholder, then name the gap outside the ad. Verify current facts before publication. Testimonials used in paid media require verified paid-media usage rights. Treat the framework as a testing structure, never a promise of results.
